author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing answers a page below the first with the first page
summary: Requesting the owner listing with a page value below 1 (zero or negative) shows the error page today. The listing must treat any such value as the first page and respond with the normal listing, as the owner's bug report states.
acceptance_criteria: given owners matching the search across several pages, when the owner listing is requested with page 0, then the response is HTTP 200 and the owner listing is shown, not the error page
given the same owners, when the owner listing is requested with a negative page value, then the response is HTTP 200 and the owner listing is shown, not the error page
given any page value below 1, when the owner listing is requested, then it shows the same first page of matches as a request for page 1, with the first page marked as the current page
non_goals: A page value beyond the last page of matches: the request names only values below 1; left open for a later slice
A page value that is not a number: not named in the request; left open
Paging in the veterinarian directory: the request names only the owner listing; left open
notes: Owner-stated requirement (intake line 1, request quoted verbatim, no decisions). The PRD adds REQ-OWN-005 to the Owner records narrative with one Done-when bullet. No existing requirement or Non-Goals row is touched, so no scope_overrides apply. One behavior, one data-driven test covering page 0 and a negative value. The veterinarian directory takes a page value too and may share the symptom. That question stays open; this slice does not depend on it.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Covered by the existing owner search-with-paging seam: the OwnerController Contracts row in docs/system-design.md § Contracts, which serves REQ-OWN-002 through the paged OwnerRepository prefix search. Cause: the private pagination helper in OwnerController.java passes page - 1 straight to PageRequest.of, which rejects a negative index with IllegalArgumentException, so page 0 or below reaches the error page. Fix: normalize the bound page parameter to at least 1 once, at the top of the /owners handler, before any arithmetic. Use the normalized value for the repository query and for the currentPage model attribute, so criterion 3 (first page marked current) holds. This is request binding, which the Web controller row of architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog allows (binds the request, delegates, selects the response). It adds no business rule to the controller. No new type, package, entry point, or dependency. Basis: grep of OwnerController.java and VetController.java (IDE oracle not connected; weaker basis than symbol resolution). The only docs/ edit is REQ-OWN-005 joining the OwnerController Implements cell.
integration_points: Framework transport: MockMvc in the existing @WebMvcTest(OwnerController.class) class, the sanctioned web-layer harness (testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy; CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy).

Repository boundary (OwnerRepository): the existing @MockitoBean in OwnerControllerTests, a framework stub taken as a conscious exception. Reason: the prd-entry pins the test to the @WebMvcTest class, which loads no JPA slice, so the real repository is out of reach. A hand-written double would have to implement the whole JpaRepository surface for one finder. Stub findByLastNameStartingWith to return a PageImpl whose total spans several pages. Assert on the captured Pageable (page index 0) and on the currentPage model attribute (1). Do not re-stub per page value.

Entry-point binding: no new entry point. GET /owners keeps its existing binding: page is a scalar request parameter, and the Owner search form stays under the existing id/*.id disallow list. This slice does not change the binding target.

patterns.description: Existing MockMvc paging tests against /owners?page=1 with a stubbed PageImpl; the new data-driven test follows their shape with page values 0 and a negative value

risks.risk: Normalizing after the subtraction, e.g. max(page - 1, 0), lets Integer.MIN_VALUE wrap to a large positive index, so the listing answers with an empty past-the-end page instead of the first page.
risks.mitigation: Clamp the one-based page to at least 1 before any arithmetic. Criterion 2 covers negative values, and a data row at Integer.MIN_VALUE pins it. security-principles.md § Trust Boundaries requires range handling before use.

risks.risk: Clamping only the query argument leaves currentPage at the raw value, so the template marks page 0 or a negative page as current. That breaks criterion 3.
risks.mitigation: Pass the one normalized value to both the query helper and addPaginationModel. The test asserts the model attribute currentPage equals 1.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; nothing to judge. Out of scope, recorded for a later slice: VetController's pagination helper has the same PageRequest.of(page - 1, ...) shape and likely shares the symptom. The prd-entry keeps that as a non-goal, and design memory records no defect row for it, per demand-driven foundation. Do not extract a shared pagination helper in this slice. The two controllers declare paging independently (system-design.md § Constants), and unifying them is a separate refactor with its own justification.

findings.description: The new test verifies the repository interaction with BDDMockito's `then(this.owners).should()`, but the same file's two existing verifications of the same `owners` mock (lines 218, 230) use plain Mockito `verify(this.owners, ...)`. This is the only `then(...).should()` call in the class, introducing a second verification idiom for the identical collaborator where the brief's consistent-with-codebase rule (docs/testing-principles.md § Test Naming note on house style) asks new tests to follow the host file's existing idiom where the brief itself is silent on which verification style to use.
findings.fix: Replace `then(this.owners).should().findByLastNameStartingWith(anyString(), requestedPage.capture());` with `verify(this.owners).findByLastNameStartingWith(anyString(), requestedPage.capture());` to match the file's existing verification idiom, and drop the now-unused `then` static import if nothing else in the file uses it.
